inspection_summary: Inspected all 1,282 normalized lines. The recoverable mathematical arc defines the de Bruijn–Newman heat family and threshold, strengthens mere zero proximity into a Lehmer-pair condition involving the surrounding zero configuration, derives local and global laws for zero motion, turns forced collision into a lower bound for the threshold, and gives a finite-sum-plus-certified-tail method for two numerical Lehmer-pair examples. Prose and logical dependencies are usable, but many displayed formulas are OCR-degraded and any formula-exact reuse requires comparison with the retained scan.

sections_inspected.mathematical_role: States the Lehmer-pair program, its implication for lower bounds on the de Bruijn–Newman constant, and the headline numerical bound.

sections_inspected.label: 1. Introduction
sections_inspected.mathematical_role: Defines the heat-deformed entire functions and threshold framework, recalls the Laguerre–Pólya characterization, defines Lehmer pairs, and states the main theorem and conditional consequence.

sections_inspected.label: 2. Movement of zeros and the de Bruijn–Newman constant
sections_inspected.mathematical_role: Develops local zero velocity, collision and simplicity results, an inverse-square zero-interaction law, and differential bounds on the environmental term.

sections_inspected.label: 3. Proofs of Theorem 1 and Corollary 1
sections_inspected.mathematical_role: Integrates the squared-gap differential equation to force a contradiction and derives the limiting consequence of infinitely many qualifying pairs.

sections_inspected.label: 4. Existence of Lehmer pairs and a numerical lower bound
sections_inspected.mathematical_role: Builds moment and tail estimates, certifies Lehmer's historic close pair, computes its threshold bound, and analyzes numerical sensitivity.

sections_inspected.label: 5. Other Lehmer pairs
sections_inspected.mathematical_role: Uses record-small gaps to choose a higher pair, certifies it by local summation plus two tail bounds, and obtains the sharper lower bound.

accepted_units.title: Heat-deformed entire functions and the threshold constant
accepted_units.why_material: The Fourier-cosine family H_t converts the real-zero question into a monotone parameter threshold: all zeros are real exactly at and above the de Bruijn–Newman constant, while the Riemann Hypothesis is the assertion that the t=0 member lies on the real-zero side. This supplies the parameter geometry used by every later collision argument.
accepted_units.context_note: Includes the definition and relation to the Riemann xi-function, de Bruijn monotonicity, Newman's threshold characterization, and the contrast with earlier lower-bound methods.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Moderate formula dependence. The defining integrals and the H_0/xi scaling are visibly OCR-degraded; use the prose-level threshold mechanism as extracted and verify exact notation against the scan.

accepted_units.title: Laguerre–Pólya membership and zero-product representation
accepted_units.why_material: The paper recasts the real-zero threshold as membership in the Laguerre–Pólya class and represents each H_t by a Hadamard product over square-summable reciprocal zeros. This bridges a global zero-location property to local derivative inequalities and convergent zero interactions.
accepted_units.context_note: Contains the class definition, equivalence H_t in the class iff t is at or above the threshold, order/type information, product factorization, zero ordering, and reciprocal-square convergence.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: High formula dependence. The product and class formula are damaged by OCR, but the prose states their roles and convergence conditions; exact factors and inequality signs need scan verification.

accepted_units.title: Lehmer pairs require a close gap relative to the entire zero environment
accepted_units.why_material: The definition improves on a raw close-pair heuristic: a consecutive simple gap is qualified only when its squared size is small relative to a convergent sum measuring interaction with all other zeros. The discussion explicitly explains that arbitrarily small gaps alone do not suffice.
accepted_units.context_note: Begins with Lehmer's historic near pair, fixes the signed indexing, defines the gap and g_k(0), explains reality and convergence of g_k, and contrasts density-driven close pairs with the stronger criterion.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: High formula dependence. The defining inequality and summand are OCR-noisy; the semantic relation is recoverable from prose, but exact constants, exclusions, and denominators must be checked against the scan.

accepted_units.title: A Lehmer pair yields an explicit lower bound and an infinite cascade forces nonnegative threshold
accepted_units.why_material: The main statement maps a local pair statistic to a source-defined negative lower bound for the de Bruijn–Newman constant, handles the case of a negative environmental sum by forcing nonreal zeros at t=0, and shows that infinitely many increasingly close Lehmer pairs would force the threshold to be nonnegative.
accepted_units.context_note: Includes Theorem 1, its explicit bound parameter, Corollary 1, the 'barely true' interpretation, and the announced numerical applications.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: High formula dependence. The OCR obscures the exact expression for the bound parameter and some inequality glyphs; preserve the conceptual implication but verify any exact formula or sign from the scan.

accepted_units.title: Local zero velocity predicts pair collision under backward heat flow
accepted_units.why_material: Implicit differentiation gives a local velocity for a simple real zero in terms of derivatives of H_t. For two close zeros separated from their neighbors, derivative signs make them approach as t decreases, motivating collision time as a lower-bound witness.
accepted_units.context_note: Includes Lemma 2.1, its implicit-function proof, the graphical sign argument, and the transition from approaching zeros to a prospective coalescence.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Moderate formula and figure dependence. The velocity quotient is OCR-degraded and the figure is only text-labeled; the direction-of-motion argument is recoverable from the accompanying prose but exact derivatives need scan verification.

accepted_units.title: A multiple real zero cannot occur above the threshold
accepted_units.why_material: A coalesced zero at parameter t_0 implies t_0 is at or below the de Bruijn–Newman threshold. The proof perturbs backward in heat time and violates a necessary Laguerre inequality; higher multiplicity is reduced by differentiation and closure of the Laguerre–Pólya class.
accepted_units.context_note: Includes Lemma 2.2, the simple-second-derivative case, the higher-multiplicity reduction, the backward-heat-equation alternative, and the t=0 consequence.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: High formula dependence. Series expansions and Laguerre expressions are OCR-damaged; the contradiction structure is clear from prose, while exact coefficients and derivative orders require scan verification.

accepted_units.title: Forward perturbation splits a double zero and all above-threshold zeros are simple
accepted_units.why_material: The local expansions show that a double real zero with nonzero second derivative splits into two simple real zeros for a small forward parameter change. Coupled with threshold membership, this yields the global simplicity statement for every t above the threshold.
accepted_units.context_note: This is the complementary local direction to the collision obstruction and culminates in Corollary 2.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: High formula dependence. The sign-change expansions are imperfectly extracted, so exact coefficients and intervals need scan verification; the stated splitting and simplicity conclusions are clear.

accepted_units.title: Zero motion as an inverse-square interaction and a gap ODE
accepted_units.why_material: Factoring out a simple zero and differentiating the Hadamard product replaces direct evaluation of H_t derivatives by a convergent sum over all other zeros. Subtracting velocities produces an ODE for a neighboring gap with a singular attraction term plus a positive environmental correction.
accepted_units.context_note: Includes the logarithmic-derivative lemma, Lemma 2.4, convergence justification, positivity above the threshold, and introduction of the tractable upper comparison g_k(t).
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Very high formula dependence. Several central summands and denominators are garbled by OCR; the inverse-square interaction, gap-law decomposition, and positivity are prose-supported, but formula-exact use requires the scan.

accepted_units.title: The environmental interaction obeys a Riccati-type lower bound
accepted_units.why_material: Differentiating the comparison sum and reorganizing single and double interactions isolates a nonnegative remainder, producing a lower differential bound for g_k. Integration then gives the upper control needed on the backward interval toward collision.
accepted_units.context_note: Covers Lemma 2.5, uniform convergence for termwise differentiation, decomposition into A(t)+B(t), positivity of B(t), comparison estimates, and the integrated bound.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Very high formula dependence. The double sums, constants, and integrated rational bound are heavily OCR-degraded; only the proof architecture and inequality roles are safe without scan verification.

accepted_units.title: Integrating the squared-gap equation forces the threshold lower bound
accepted_units.why_material: Assuming the threshold lies below the pair-derived bound keeps both zeros real and simple throughout an interval. An integrating factor and the environmental estimate then force the squared gap to become negative at the proposed endpoint, contradicting simplicity and proving the lower bound.
accepted_units.context_note: This is the central causal chain from a static Lehmer-pair certificate at t=0 to an unavoidable collision obstruction under backward flow.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: High formula dependence. The integrating-factor formulas and constants are OCR-noisy, but the contradiction through a negative squared gap is explicit in the prose; scan verification is required for exact algebra.

accepted_units.title: Infinitely many shrinking Lehmer gaps force a nonnegative threshold
accepted_units.why_material: The pair-derived lower bound is rewritten using the dimensionless product of squared gap and environmental term. Monotonicity shows the bound tends to zero exactly when the certified gaps do, so a sequence of lower bounds approaching zero forces the threshold to be nonnegative.
accepted_units.context_note: This proves Corollary 1 and turns repeated local near-collisions into a global limiting statement.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: High formula dependence. The scalar monotonicity formula is damaged, though the equivalence of the two limits and conclusion are stated; exact normalization needs scan verification.

accepted_units.title: A moment ratio fixes the total reciprocal-square zero mass
accepted_units.why_material: Comparing the Hadamard product with the Taylor expansion expresses the total reciprocal-square sum over zeros through low-order moments of the Fourier kernel, allowing a rigorously controlled global constant to enter later tail estimates.
accepted_units.context_note: Includes Lemma 4.1, the product/Taylor comparison, positivity of moments, cited numerical accuracy, and the evaluated constant.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Very high formula dependence and externally computed numeric input. The identity and moment values are OCR-sensitive and must be checked against the scan and cited table before exact reuse.

accepted_units.title: Finite zero sums can be completed by an explicit tail bound
accepted_units.why_material: The full environmental interaction g_k(0) is decomposed into a finite partial sum and a remainder. Evenness, zero ordering, reciprocal-square mass, and a bound on possible imaginary parts control the omitted tail and prove convergence, creating a reusable numerical certification pattern.
accepted_units.context_note: Covers Lemma 4.2 and the derivation of its remainder estimate, including treatment compatible with hypothetical nonreal zeros.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Very high formula dependence. The displayed remainder bound and intermediate products are substantially garbled; the finite-plus-tail architecture is recoverable, but exact inequalities require scan verification.

accepted_units.title: The historic Lehmer pair is certified and converted into a threshold bound
accepted_units.why_material: A close pair whose neighboring zeros are relatively distant is tested by summing 14,999 zero contributions and bounding the remainder with the global reciprocal-square constant. The resulting strict Lehmer inequality feeds Theorem 1 to produce a numerical lower bound.
accepted_units.context_note: Includes pair selection, gap and neighbor data, finite-sum provenance and precision, the tail estimate, Lemma 4.3, and Theorem 2.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Very high dependence on OCR-sensitive formulas and cited numerical tables. The certification logic is clear, but indices, decimal exponents, constants, and inequality directions must be checked against the scan and source data.

accepted_units.title: The pair-derived bound is dominated by the squared gap
accepted_units.why_material: Order-of-magnitude changes to the upper estimate for the environmental term barely affect the first significant digits of the threshold bound. A series expansion explains this stability: the leading contribution depends on minus one eighth of the squared gap.
accepted_units.context_note: This separates the geometrically dominant close-gap signal from the less sensitive environmental correction in the example.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: High formula and decimal-exponent dependence. The qualitative robustness comparison is prose-supported, but all numerical values and expansion coefficients need scan verification.

accepted_units.title: Record-small consecutive gaps prioritize candidate Lehmer pairs
accepted_units.why_material: Among record-setting consecutive zero gaps, early entries need not satisfy the stronger Lehmer condition, but the dominance of the squared-gap term makes the smallest available gap a rational candidate for the best lower bound. This distinguishes candidate retrieval from certification.
accepted_units.context_note: Defines the record-gap list, notes that close pairs are not automatically Lehmer pairs, selects the final pair, and records the precision and provenance of the zeros.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Moderate numerical dependence. The selection principle is clear, while the exact indices, gap, and claimed decimal accuracy should be verified against the scan and underlying data.

accepted_units.title: A high-index pair is certified by a local window plus two tail controls
accepted_units.why_material: The environmental sum for the selected high pair is partitioned into 5,000 nearby zeros on each side, a finite remote block, and the far tail. Crude but explicit bounds on both omitted regions suffice to establish the strict Lehmer inequality.
accepted_units.context_note: Includes Lemma 5.1, the three-part decomposition, the two remainder estimates, the combined upper bound on g_k(0), and the final gap-times-environment check.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Very high formula and computed-data dependence. OCR badly damages summation limits and exponents; exact certification must be reconstructed from the scan and Odlyzko data, though the partition-and-bound method is explicit in prose.

accepted_units.title: A much smaller certified gap sharpens the lower bound and motivates an infinite-pair route
accepted_units.why_material: Applying the general theorem to the high-index certificate yields the paper's sharper numerical lower bound. The comparison with the leading squared-gap term again shows robustness, and the conclusion proposes that increasingly close certified pairs could continue improving bounds and realize the infinite-pair scenario.
accepted_units.context_note: Contains Theorem 3, the rounded and more precise forms of the result, leading-term comparison, and the concluding connection to Lehmer's prediction.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: High numerical and formula dependence. OCR loses minus signs and decimal exponents in places; exact bound values and normalization require scan verification, while the qualitative conclusion is clear.

within_source_synthesis_candidates.title: From a static close pair to a dynamical threshold obstruction
within_source_synthesis_candidates.claim: A gap is informative only relative to its surrounding zero configuration; that certified static imbalance controls the gap ODE strongly enough that backward heat flow would force collision unless the de Bruijn–Newman threshold lies above an explicit pair-derived value.
within_source_synthesis_candidates.limit: This synthesis is conditional on the source's OCR-sensitive formulas and constants; formula-exact training material needs scan verification.

within_source_synthesis_candidates.title: Collision, splitting, and simplicity form a local phase-boundary picture
within_source_synthesis_candidates.claim: At a multiple real zero, backward perturbation exits the Laguerre–Pólya region while forward perturbation produces two simple real zeros, so multiplicity marks a local boundary event and all strictly above-threshold zeros must be simple.
within_source_synthesis_candidates.limit: The extracted Taylor coefficients are unreliable; only the qualitative bifurcation and stated corollary are secure without the scan.

within_source_synthesis_candidates.title: Global analytic identities make finite zero computations certifiable
within_source_synthesis_candidates.claim: A moment-derived total reciprocal-square mass converts incomplete zero tables into rigorous certificates: compute a finite interaction sum, bound omitted regions analytically, then test the strict Lehmer inequality.
within_source_synthesis_candidates.limit: Both examples rely on external zero tables and OCR-damaged numerical exponents; provenance and scan-level reconstruction are necessary before reproduction.

within_source_synthesis_candidates.title: Candidate retrieval by tiny gaps is distinct from Lehmer certification
within_source_synthesis_candidates.claim: Record-small gaps efficiently rank candidates because the pair-derived bound is led by the squared gap, but only an environmental-sum certificate upgrades a candidate to a Lehmer pair.
within_source_synthesis_candidates.limit: The heuristic is demonstrated on two familiar numerical cases and is not evidence that every record gap qualifies.

within_source_synthesis_candidates.title: Local certificates can accumulate toward a global nonnegativity statement
within_source_synthesis_candidates.claim: Each Lehmer pair supplies a negative lower bound, and an infinite sequence of certified gaps shrinking to zero would make those bounds approach zero, forcing the threshold to be nonnegative while remaining compatible with the Riemann Hypothesis at equality.
within_source_synthesis_candidates.limit: The source does not prove the existence of infinitely many Lehmer pairs; its conclusion is explicitly predictive.
